sourceCitation: ICMR-NIN, Nutrient Requirements for Indians, 2020 (RDA/EAR report)
notes: Transcribed from the ICMR-NIN 2020 recommendations for Indian adults.
These values are PENDING the nutrition review packet (scope doc §0.6, §37 item 8) and
ADR-010 stays Proposed until that review happens. They are here so the app can derive
micronutrient targets at all; they are not a substitute for the review.
Sodium is WHO guidance (<2,000 mg/day) rather than an ICMR RDA — it is a limit, not an
intake to reach, and it is scored as a ceiling.
Sugar and saturated fat are absent on purpose: WHO states both as a share of energy, so
they are derived per-profile in target_derivation.dart rather than looked up here.
One adult band (19+) rather than 19-59 and 60+: ICMR's adult recommendations for these
nutrients are given against a reference body weight, and inventing a second band would
imply a distinction this transcription cannot support.
PREGNANCY AND LACTATION (added with the week planner). Only the nutrients whose
requirement actually changes carry a lifestage row. Everything else falls back to the
adult row of the same age and sex, which ProfileDao.referencesFor does explicitly — so
the absence of a row here means 'unchanged', never 'no target'.
THESE FIGURES NEED CHECKING AGAINST THE REPORT BEFORE ANYONE RELIES ON THEM. They carry
the same pending_review status as the adult values above and are transcribed at the same
confidence. Specifically unresolved, and deliberately left without a row rather than
guessed at: calcium, zinc, vitamin A, vitamin C, vitamin D, thiamin, riboflavin, niacin,
vitamin B6, magnesium and vitamin E in pregnancy and lactation. Each of those currently
falls back to its adult value, which is a defensible default and is not a claim that
ICMR states the same number.
Iron in pregnancy is LOWER than the non-pregnant adult female value, not higher. That is
what ICMR-NIN 2020 states, and it is not a transcription error: menstrual losses stop.
It is called out here because it is the one number a reviewer will assume is wrong.
Energy and protein increments are not in this file. They are additions to a number
derived per-profile, so they live in target_derivation.dart with saturated fat and sugar,
for the same reason: a table keyed by age and sex cannot express 'plus 350'.
